title: The Gobi Desert
text: The Gobi Desert is a large cold desert and grassland biome in East Asia, covering approximately 1.3 million square kilometers across northern and northwestern China and southern Mongolia. Unlike the Sahara, the Gobi is not primarily sandy — about 5% is covered in sand dunes. Most of the desert is covered with bare rock. The Gobi is known for its fossil richness; paleontologists have discovered significant dinosaur eggs and skeletons there. Temperatures in the Gobi range from -40°C in winter to over 45°C in summer. The Gobi is expanding due to desertification, driven by climate change and overgrazing, threatening agricultural land in China.
